title: Saliency-Regularized Deep Multi-Task Learning

problem.claim: Existing multi-task learning approaches need to improve task generalization while representing task relations and sharing knowledge across tasks.

gap.claim: Shallow methods handle only pre-defined features, while deep methods obscure task relations and predefine which layers and neurons share across tasks instead of learning sharing adaptively.

contributions.claim: A multi-task learning framework jointly learns latent features and explicit task relations by complementing shallow and deep multi-task learning.
Task relations are modeled as the similarity between tasks' input gradients, with a theoretical analysis of their equivalency.
A multi-task learning objective uses a new regularizer to explicitly learn task relations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis shows that the generalizability error has been reduced through the proposed regularizer.
Experiments on several multi-task learning and image classification benchmarks demonstrate the method's effectiveness, efficiency, and reasonableness in learned task-relation patterns.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-task learning shares knowledge among multiple tasks to improve generalization.
Shallow and deep multi-task learning have complementary limitations involving feature handling, task-relation transparency, and adaptive sharing.
The proposed framework jointly learns latent features and explicit task relations, modeling relations through input-gradient similarity and a new regularizer.
Theoretical analysis reports reduced generalizability error due to the regularizer.
Benchmark experiments report effectiveness, efficiency, and reasonable learned task-relation patterns.

source_observation.claim: The method represents task relations using similarity between tasks' input gradients.

interpretation.claim: Input-gradient similarity can provide an explicit signal for task relatedness.

application.claim: When designing multi-task models, consider gradient-based relation signals to guide task sharing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether gradient similarity is appropriate for tasks or data types beyond those evaluated.

source_observation.claim: The proposed regularizer is reported to reduce generalizability error and produce reasonable task-relation patterns.

interpretation.claim: Explicit relation regularization may improve both generalization and the plausibility of learned sharing.

application.claim: Use explicit task-relation regularization when adaptive sharing and interpretable relation patterns are desired.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the error definition, baseline comparisons, or quantitative effect sizes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the regularizer's mathematical form.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, or benchmark names.
The abstract does not detail the theoretical assumptions or equivalency result.
The abstract does not identify the computational cost underlying the efficiency claim.
